title: Kumaraṉ’s Message
paragraphs: The function marking the birth of a child
Kumaraṉ and Kumari’s house Was visited by Vēḷaṉ from Kōṭṭai street. He joyfully gifted the chain made of cow’s horn.
“What Vēḷaṉ? Quite uncharacteristic of you to have come all alone? Why didn’t you bring your woman?” They eagerly enquired.
“We have not been on talking terms for some days. You have often been grumbling about my being issueless.’ So saying, She had gone to grandma’s house. Six weeks have passed since then.”

To dispel the cloud of sadness from his face, On the very next day, Kumaraṉ accompanied by Vēḷaṉ, went to grandma’s house, And spoke to his wife: “Is it sulking or growling? If you remain separated for being issueless,
Would you be gifted with a child?
My parents used to say that I was born ten years after their marriage. If my parents had also remained parted in sulks for having been issueless, How could I have been born?
Now also, there are quarrels and sulks marking our conjugal life.

I ventured to a foreign country in pursuit of wealth. ‘My life would be shrouded in darkness, therefore I would also come.’ She insisted. How can I change the convention against women taking up voyage?

With her eyes flooded with tears, She quarrelled and remained silent for a few days. I could not change the age-old custom of ancestors, But I changed my plan of going on a voyage, I travelled to the nearby capital city for training in warfare for ten days.
‘You assured me that there wouldn’t be any separation. I didn’t know then that you were lying.’ She fired a letter on the fifth day itself.
Then, what work could I have there? I beat a hasty retreat midway, To wipe off her misery caused by parting.
Compromise has never been a one way path in my house.
I had committed a big blunder when she gave birth to my son. A fury she did become! But on my apology she forgot what had happened.

Unlike in my case, No male chauvinistic blunder has happened here. Therefore you should forget the quarrel with your man. You should extend a whole-hearted cooperation. May you be blessed with the fruit of your thousand year crop, your married life!”
Such of these arguments and many more I presented before her. “Nothing equals the bliss of married life. The life of the householder is a virtue unto itself.
And a finer thing it would be were it to be freed of blame.” I also said.

“Vēḷaṉ! This is for you also: ‘Even if there is no child in the house, We should toil like the child of the nation’. You should make a vow, And with a bright and beaming face, Lead a life like a sword and its sheath.”
Vēḷaṉ and his wife expressed their gratitude to Kumaraṉ And said, “We shall live together ever.”

> As he ends the affliction of the two women > [The heroine and his concubine] > Who stand grieving at his parting; > > As he stands in distress intense > Over his protracted separation from the heroine; > > As he ponders taking the hard tract > Which he had gone through in the past; > > As he realizes the overriding hold of love; > As he fears the heroine’s affliction > When parting from her intervenes; > > As he fails to keep his word to her > [As regards his promise of return in a given season > And as regards his promise of non-separation]; > > As he responds to the words of credulity of the confidante > Who urges him to take the heroine with him, > And who makes many a plea of this kind; > > As he feels the pain of separation > While setting off to a foreign land; > > As he ponders breaking his journey and returning home; > The feel of joy that attends > As he is homeward after the mission; > > ....
(Poruḷatikāram : Karpiyal, verse 5)
